$comment: MODEL CAPABILITY / COST CACHE — deliberately EMPTY.
This file used to ship with model ids and prices written from an author's memory. That was a
bug, and it bit: the agent read the invented table, proposed a model that did not exist, and the
human was told 'that model is not available'. A file whose whole purpose is 'do not trust stale
knowledge' cannot itself be populated from stale knowledge.
So it ships empty, on purpose. POPULATE IT FROM THE LIVE PROVIDER at setup time:
An empty cache is honest. A confidently wrong cache is worse than none, because the agent will
SUBSCRIPTION MODE: ignore this file entirely. The model is whatever the TUI agent runs — ask it,

reasoning.used_for: deciding what to do, planning work, judging whether an outcome was good
reasoning.guidance: Worth paying for. This is where the system creates or destroys value — a bad decision costs far more than the tokens saved by making it cheaply.

working.used_for: doing the work — drafting, transforming, writing, calling tools
working.guidance: Most of the volume lives here. Competence at a sane price.

cheap.guidance: High volume, low judgment. Spending reasoning-tier money here is the most common way to burn a budget on nothing.

cost_model.$comment: Used to show the human a monthly estimate BEFORE they commit to a budget in 05-budget.md. A number they can see beats a lecture about model quality. Web search is metered separately — look up the current per-search price and add it in; at research-heavy cadences it can exceed the token cost.
cost_model.formula: monthly_usd = cycles_per_day * 30 * ( sum_over_tiers(calls * (in_tokens/1e6 * price_in + out_tokens/1e6 * price_out)) + searches_per_cycle * price_per_search )
